summary: The note explains how community learning centers (CLCs) use collaboration and partnerships with local businesses, nonprofits, volunteers, and digital tools to expand education beyond public schools. It walks through steps for building partnerships: identifying needs, mapping assets, forming a shared vision, creating frameworks, launching programs, gathering feedback, and sustaining relationships. Examples from various named CLCs illustrate each step, with the goal of fostering lifelong learning.
one_line: Community learning centers build partnerships with local organizations, volunteers, and digital platforms through a stepwise process to support lifelong learning.
key_facts: Community learning centers (CLCs) emerged as a response to the need for supplementary educational support and to bridge school resources with community assets; the note says a pronounced shift occurred after September 1, 2023.
Jennifer Parker, Director of the Elmwood Community Learning Center, called her center "a crucible for learning and collaboration."
Mary Gonzales, a community organizer for the Riverdale district, described an asset mapping workshop held on October 14, 2023.
On November 2, 2023, at the Sunrise Valley CLC's stakeholders meeting, principal Alex Davis said a shared vision unites stakeholders around youth leadership, adult learning, or community wellness.
The Lakeside CLC entered a partnership agreement with the local Rotary Club on December 1, 2023, defining a timetable for joint literacy workshops and monthly progress meetings.
TechForward partnered with the Downtown CLC to start a coding boot camp on January 15, 2024; TechForward supplied instructors and equipment while the CLC managed enrollment and facilities.
The Midtown CLC holds quarterly reviews with its partners so programs can be adjusted in real time; coordinator Chris Thorne said the feedback loop keeps programs relevant and effective.
The Meadow Hill CLC hosts an annual "Partnership Celebration" to maintain enthusiasm and appreciation among stakeholders.
Laura Simmons, volunteer coordinator at the Eastbridge Center, called volunteers "the lifeblood of our center."
The Spring Valley CLC recently launched a digital collaboration portal to streamline management and offering of joint programs.
Asset assessment involves mapping local businesses, non-profit organizations, cultural institutions, and service providers.
A partnership framework includes mutual goals, defined roles and expectations, and communication channels.
